title: Where Is Energy Stored? Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav pulls his phone charger out of the wall, yet its little light stays on for a moment and then fades. Where is that energy coming from? In this animated lesson we meet the three passive components and what each does with energy: a resistor turns it into heat, a capacitor stores it in an electric field and an inductor stores it in a magnetic field.

On a live breadboard a capacitor charges from a battery and then lights a lamp with no battery in the loop, while the oscilloscope draws the capacitor voltage and the current together. We derive U = 1/2 CV^2 step by step from the area under the voltage-charge graph, work out the energy in a 100 microfarad capacitor at 12 V (and see why doubling the voltage gives four times the energy), then meet the inductor and U = 1/2 LI^2. Then the exam trap (the battery gives QV but the capacitor keeps only half), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 30 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).

In this video:
0:00 The charger light that will not switch off
0:19 Resistor, capacitor, inductor: who stores energy?
0:36 Charging and discharging a capacitor on a breadboard
1:22 Resistors spend energy, capacitors and inductors store it
1:27 Deriving U = 1/2 CV^2
2:13 Worked example: 100 microfarads at 12 V
2:42 Energy in an inductor: U = 1/2 LI^2
3:20 Exam trap: half the energy is lost
3:37 Where it is asked
3:51 Practice question
4:32 Formula card
